chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah Al-Qurashi, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdullah Al-Nawfaly, from Zadan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: 'If I had authority over the markets of the Muslims, I would have removed this wine from them, meaning the fermented drink (fuqaa').

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعَ: Fuqaa, a specific type of fermented drink mentioned in the hadith

ai.seo_question: What is 'fuqaa' and how did the Imams view its status as wine?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses a desire to ban 'fuqaa' from Muslim markets if he held political authority, highlighting its status as a distinct, widely consumed fermented beverage. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on preventing the gradual intoxication associated with such drinks, even if they are not pure wine, thereby protecting the community from the slippery slope of alcohol consumption. The statement underscores the practical application of *khamr* (intoxicant) rulings in public commerce and social governance.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya and someone else, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Abdullah Al Qarashy, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdullah Al Nowfaly, from Zadaan, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Had there been the authority (rule) for me<sup>asws</sup> upon the markets of the Muslims, I would have lifted these wines from them, meaning the fermented drinks’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Husayn ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Qarashiy certain persons of our people from abu ‘Abd Allah al-Nawfaliy from Zadhan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If I had control over the market places of the Muslims I would ban this wine, that is, al-Fuqa ’ (beer).”’
